findings.title: Account deletion can erase the data, then silently leave the account in place

evidence.detail: On requires-recent-login the jobs and entries are already deleted. If reauthenticate() returns false (the user cancels or fails), the code falls through with no error, no message and no sign-out. The account survives with its data wiped, and the user is never told.
Data is deleted before user.delete(), so a failure at the second step is not recoverable or retryable from the user's side.

The default re-auth dialog is built from authProviders, which holds only EmailAuthProvider. An anonymous user (offered on the sign-in screen) has no credential to re-enter, so this path cannot complete for them.

fix.recipe: When reauthenticate() returns false, show a message that the account was not deleted and that the data is already removed. For anonymous users, either skip re-auth and call user.delete() after a fresh signInAnonymously(), or tell them to sign out and in again. Alternatively reauthenticate first and delete data second. Add a widget test for the cancelled re-auth path.

findings.guideline: Apple 1.5 Developer Information; 5.1.1(i) Privacy Policy contact
findings.title: The only user contact is a confidential GitLab issue, and the listing has no support URL

evidence.detail: Contact for questions and requests is a confidential issue on a GitLab project. Ordinary App Store users cannot be expected to have a GitLab account, and the link points at a hackathon project path.
The fallback for users who cannot sign in (so cannot use in-app deletion) is the same GitLab issue form. They have no practical way to request deletion.
The listing defines privacy_policy_url and account_deletion_url but no support_url or contact email. App Store Connect requires a Support URL and reviewers check that it works.

fix.recipe: Provide a monitored support email or a public support page. Add support_url to store/listing.yaml, and replace the GitLab link in privacy.html and delete-account.html with that contact. Redeploy the Cloud Run legal pages.
